original_skill.name: verify-usage-separator-formatting
steps: Run the dedicated public test action BEFORE any edit to capture the original broken behavior; record the exact failing assertion output, including diff hints and any 'Skipping N identical leading' truncation.

Read the failure diff carefully: hidden differences (trailing spaces, escape fragments, off-by-count positions like 'done=8' vs 'done=11') are often masked by truncation. Split actual vs expected and identify whether the defect is in the computed value, the rendering, or the width/escape handling.

Identify every named feature state and output surface in the issue (e.g. visible vs hidden display, color enabled vs disabled, manual vs iterator updates, multiple CSI forms including colon-form RGB). The supplied public suite typically contains one test per registered state — treat each named state as a separate check, not as covered by a passing sibling.

Locate the assembly/update point: for separator or optional-fragment issues, emit separators only between non-empty parts; for batched-progress under-counting, flush any remaining pending partial batch when the progress bar finishes (both explicit finish and context-manager exit) so hidden and visible paths share correct accounting; for width bugs, make the escape-stripping pattern cover all valid CSI forms while leaving adjacent text and incomplete sequences intact.
Fix the root cause once, covering all named states; do not special-case literal strings, widths, or test names.

When behavior is uncertain, run a small isolated probe through the library API (e.g. import the width/escape helpers and print term_len/strip_ansi on representative sequences) before editing, to confirm which inputs are mishandled; keep probes read-only.

Run the dedicated public test action after the edit and check EACH named state's result individually; one passing and one failing state means the fix is incomplete (observed: hidden-state 'done=8' persisted while the enabled state passed after the first edit).

When both states pass, save a green checkpoint of the verified editable snapshot; if any later edit regresses a state, use restore_checkpoint to return to the saved green rather than re-deriving the fix, then re-verify with the public test action.
Reserve the final step for a full clean verification run of the exact public command; stop editing after a verified pass and submit only from that state.
verification: The dedicated public test action passes after the final edit, with every registered named state (e.g. disabled and enabled) reported passing individually, not just an aggregate exit code.

Every state and surface named in the issue is explicitly checked: hidden display stays silent with the correct final summary; visible display reaches the full position with normal position/percent formatting; styled and plain renderings wrap at the same visible columns with styles preserved and no escape fragments when color is off.
Behavior for already-correct inputs (non-empty fragments, complete non-batched updates, plain text) is unchanged — verified by the paired disabled/enabled assertions, not visual inspection.
A clean run of the exact public command on the final snapshot was performed (saved green) and no edit follows it without re-verification; the restore path was exercised only if a regression appeared.
No step or command budget exhausted at submission; post-success edits without a re-verification run are not allowed.
